post.description:
Make the account match its bank. Send `new_balance` (what the bank says it holds) or
`amount` (what to add, negative to take away). The difference is recorded as a dated income or
expense (a "Balance adjustment") that changes the balance and its history from that date, but
is **not** income or spending in any total, report or budget. Delete it to undo it.

Close an account you no longer use. Its transactions stay in the history, but it leaves
the overview, the totals and the pickers. Undo with `unarchive`.

get.description: The file itself, shown in the browser unless `download` is true.

post.description:
Turn two-factor off. Needs your password and a code (or a recovery code). Your other
sign-ins end.

Turn two-factor on with a code from the app. The recovery codes in the answer are shown
once. Your other sign-ins end: they were made without a second factor.

Make a new set of recovery codes (the old ones stop working), shown once. Needs your
password and a code. Your other sign-ins end.

Start setting up an authenticator app: a secret and its QR code (the same ones if setup was
already started and not finished). Nothing changes for sign-in until `/auth/2fa/enable` has seen
a right code.

OAuth2 password flow: send `username` (the email) and `password` as form fields. Ten wrong
passwords for one email, or thirty from one address, in fifteen minutes answer 429.

The second step of signing in: the challenge from `/auth/login` and a code from the
authenticator app (or an unused recovery code).
End this sign-in. The token stops working at once, even if someone copied it.

Change your password. Needs the current one, and a code when two-factor is on. Your other
sign-ins end. Wrong current passwords count toward the same limit as signing in, so a stolen
session cannot be used to guess the password.
